issue.title: [google_cloud_rpc] Fix _makeStreamingRequest non-SSE EOF buffering and mid-stream error handling
issue.body_html:
Context & Problem

While PR #339 adds resilient gRPC bidirectional streaming pull specifically for handwritten pkgs/google_cloud_pubsub, all generated server-streaming REST RPCs (such as Vertex AI streamGenerateContent, Gemini streamGenerateContent, and Firestore Listen) rely on ServiceClient._makeStreamingRequest() in generated/google_cloud_rpc/lib/service_client.dart (lines 177–241).

Currently, _makeStreamingRequest() has two runtime issues:

  1. Non-SSE application/json Responses Buffer Until EOF (service_client.dart:210-217):

    • When enableSse: false (or when a Google API returns a chunked JSON array [obj1, obj2, ...] with Content-Type: application/json instead of text/event-stream), lines 213–216 execute: 
      final responseBody = await response.stream.bytesToString();
final json = (jsonDecode(responseBody) as List)
    .cast<Map<String, dynamic>>();
yield* Stream.fromIterable(json);
    • Awaiting response.stream.bytesToString() blocks until the entire HTTP stream reaches EOF before decoding or yielding the first item, defeating incremental streaming for non-SSE streaming endpoints (see also googleapis/librarian#2490 and googleapis/librarian#5533).

  2. Mid-Stream SSE Error Frames Are Silently Decoded as Empty Messages (service_client.dart:230-240):

    • When Content-Type: text/event-stream is active, an HTTP 200 OK response header is sent before streaming begins. If an error occurs mid-stream (e.g., quota exhaustion, deadline exceeded, or upstream disconnect), Google APIs emit an SSE data: {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "status": ...}} JSON frame.
    • Currently, lines 236–238 decode the data: payload and yield json directly to the generated method's .map(ResponseType.fromJson). Because ResponseType does not have an error field, ResponseType.fromJson silently ignores the "error" key and yields a default/empty ResponseType message instead of throwing a ServiceException.

Proposed Solution

  1. Detect and Throw ServiceException on Mid-Stream Error Payloads:
    • In _makeStreamingRequest(), inspect each decoded Map<String, dynamic> item (both in the SSE data: loop and JSON array stream) for a top-level 'error' object matching google.rpc.Status / Google REST error format (matching the check in ServiceException.fromHttpResponse in lib/src/exceptions.dart:105-110), and throw the corresponding ServiceException.
  2. Incremental Framing for application/json Streaming Responses:
    • Replace the full-stream await response.stream.bytesToString() buffer in the case 'application/json': branch with an incremental JSON array element splitter/decoder so elements in [obj1, obj2, ...] are yielded as chunks arrive over response.stream.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Mid-stream SSE data: {"error": ...} frames (and chunked JSON array error elements) throw a ServiceException on the returned Stream rather than yielding an empty/default response message.
  • application/json streaming responses (enableSse: false) yield array elements incrementally as HTTP chunks arrive instead of buffering until EOF.

issue.body:
### Context & Problem

While PR #339 adds resilient gRPC bidirectional streaming pull specifically for handwritten `pkgs/google_cloud_pubsub`, all generated server-streaming REST RPCs (such as Vertex AI `streamGenerateContent`, Gemini `streamGenerateContent`, and Firestore `Listen`) rely on `ServiceClient._makeStreamingRequest()` in `generated/google_cloud_rpc/lib/service_client.dart` (lines 177–241).

Currently, `_makeStreamingRequest()` has two runtime issues:

1. **Non-SSE `application/json` Responses Buffer Until EOF (`service_client.dart:210-217`)**:
   - When `enableSse: false` (or when a Google API returns a chunked JSON array `[obj1, obj2, ...]` with `Content-Type: application/json` instead of `text/event-stream`), lines 213–216 execute:
     ```dart
     final responseBody = await response.stream.bytesToString();
     final json = (jsonDecode(responseBody) as List)
         .cast<Map<String, dynamic>>();
     yield* Stream.fromIterable(json);
     ```
   - Awaiting `response.stream.bytesToString()` blocks until the entire HTTP stream reaches EOF before decoding or yielding the first item, defeating incremental streaming for non-SSE streaming endpoints (see also `googleapis/librarian#2490` and `googleapis/librarian#5533`).

2. **Mid-Stream SSE Error Frames Are Silently Decoded as Empty Messages (`service_client.dart:230-240`)**:
   - When `Content-Type: text/event-stream` is active, an HTTP `200 OK` response header is sent before streaming begins. If an error occurs mid-stream (e.g., quota exhaustion, deadline exceeded, or upstream disconnect), Google APIs emit an SSE `data: {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "status": ...}}` JSON frame.
   - Currently, lines 236–238 decode the `data: ` payload and `yield json` directly to the generated method's `.map(ResponseType.fromJson)`. Because `ResponseType` does not have an `error` field, `ResponseType.fromJson` silently ignores the `"error"` key and yields a default/empty `ResponseType` message instead of throwing a `ServiceException`.

### Proposed Solution

1. **Detect and Throw `ServiceException` on Mid-Stream Error Payloads**:
   - In `_makeStreamingRequest()`, inspect each decoded `Map<String, dynamic>` item (both in the SSE `data:` loop and JSON array stream) for a top-level `'error'` object matching `google.rpc.Status` / Google REST error format (matching the check in `ServiceException.fromHttpResponse` in `lib/src/exceptions.dart:105-110`), and throw the corresponding `ServiceException`.
2. **Incremental Framing for `application/json` Streaming Responses**:
   - Replace the full-stream `await response.stream.bytesToString()` buffer in the `case 'application/json':` branch with an incremental JSON array element splitter/decoder so elements in `[obj1, obj2, ...]` are yielded as chunks arrive over `response.stream`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Mid-stream SSE `data: {"error": ...}` frames (and chunked JSON array error elements) throw a `ServiceException` on the returned `Stream` rather than yielding an empty/default response message.
- [ ] `application/json` streaming responses (`enableSse: false`) yield array elements incrementally as HTTP chunks arrive instead of buffering until EOF.

issue.title: sidekick(dart generator): Only generate streaming method implementations for white-listed methods
issue.body_html:
Currently all methods that can stream results (e.g. StreamGenerateContent) have a corresponding generated Dart binding, e.g.

  /// Generates a [streamed response](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/text-generation?lang=python#generate-a-text-stream)
  /// from the model given an input `GenerateContentRequest`.
  Stream<GenerateContentResponse> streamGenerateContent(
    GenerateContentRequest request,
  ) {
    final url = Uri.https(_host, '/v1/${request.model}:streamGenerateContent');
    return _client
        .postStreaming(url, body: request)
        .map(GenerateContentResponse.fromJson);
  }

But not all streaming methods support Server-sent events (SSE), which is the implementation supported by Dart.

So instead whitelist streamed methods known to support SSE.

issue.title: feat(dart): support a SSE allowlist
issue.body_html:
Not all APIs with results marked stream support Server-Sent Events (SSE).

This PR adds a configuration option to enable SSE for the API.

  - name: google_cloud_showcase_v1beta1
    apis:
      - path: schema/google/showcase/v1beta1
    dart:
      supports_sse: true

Based on this configuration, a boolean configuration option, enableSse, is passed to the transport layer:

  Stream<GenerateContentResponse> streamGenerateContent(
    GenerateContentRequest request,
  ) {
    final url = _endPoint.replace(
      path: '/v1beta/${request.model}:streamGenerateContent',
    );
    return _client
        .postStreaming(url, body: request, enableSse: true)
        .map(GenerateContentResponse.fromJson);
  }

enableSse is used to decide whether to request SSE from the server.

issue.title: feat(pubsub): add resilient parallel streaming pull
issue.body_html:
Adds resilient parallel streaming pull to Subscription.streamingPull
and routes batched acknowledgments and deadline modifications over
active streams when available.

  • Subscription.streamingPull opens maxConcurrentStreams parallel
    StreamingPull connections and multiplexes their messages onto a
    single returned Stream<ReceivedMessage>.
  • Reconnects automatically with exponential backoff (RetryRunner) when
    a stream fails with a retryable error or closes unexpectedly, and
    resets the retry state once a stream receives a message or remains
    connected for at least 15 seconds.
  • When maxConcurrentStreams > 1, an individual stream exhausting its
    retries does not terminate the combined stream while sibling streams
    remain active.
  • Batched acknowledgments and deadline modifications from
    Subscription.acknowledge, Subscription.modifyAckDeadline,
    ReceivedMessage.acknowledge, and
    ReceivedMessage.modifyAckDeadline are written to an active
    StreamingPull request stream when one is open, falling back to
    unary RPCs with retry when no stream is active.
  • Propagates pause and resume across all active underlying streams,
    and in Subscription.close() cancels active streaming pulls before
    flushing pending batches via unary RPCs.
  • Adds PubSub.streamingPullWithStream for bidirectional
    request/response stream management.

Stacked on #292.
